abstract: OpenAI's preprint, whose main theorem states that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>7/8$, and Liu's improvements work with residue symbols over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. One input is a second-moment bound for Möbius-weighted sums of residue symbols, proved through Patterson's cubic theta function. We study the quartic analogue over $\mathbb Q(i)$, where no such theta description is available. For primary squarefree $c$ with split prime factors, the normalised quartic Gauss sum satisfies $\gamma_1(c)^2=\mu(c)\,(c/|c|)\,\chi_c(-1)$, a form of the classical square formula, so it carries the Möbius function in its square. A row twist carries $\mu$ in this way only in one orientation, and there the rows are Gauss sums at cube numerators. For every row with an odd prime factor to the first power, the residue of the quartic theta series vanishes there; for the $\asymp X^{1/2}$ rows with squarefull odd part it need not. We prove that the mean square of the carrier sums over rows of norm about $X$ is $\ll X^{2+\theta+\varepsilon}$ whenever twisted quartic Möbius large sieves have excess $B^{\theta}$ uniformly in twists of conductor up to $X^{1/2-2\theta}$ and in coprimality conditions of norm up to $2X$. Without the last restriction the hypothesis is false. The largest shortfall occurs where rows and columns both have norm about $X$, and there the Möbius sieve is the Poisson dual of the carrier energy itself. De Faveri's quartic large sieve gives $X^{9/4+\varepsilon}$, and GRH gives $X^{2+\varepsilon}$; heuristically, a zero-density estimate for the quartic family with exponent $\kappa$ gives excess $\max(0,1-2/\kappa)$. In a transcription of Liu's optimisation, which we label a model and state in full, every admissible point has exponent at least $9/10$ for the generic excess $1/4$, and beating Liu's $0.87446830769$ needs $\theta<0.18617$. Numerically, up to $X=2^{15}$, the carrier energy is within $6\%$ of the exact random-phase expectation. No zero-free region is proved.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Corrections only, following the reviews of version 1 and of the first version-2 submission. Step 3 now reads mu(c_j') = mu(e) mu(b_j); the two factors mu(e) cancel, so the argument is unchanged. V >= 0 and W real are stated, and the zero-frequency main term is distinguished from the full c_1 = c_2 contribution. The threshold is stated as theta < 0.18617, with 0.186 used as a sufficient value, and the endpoint values of gamma are handled by limits. The GRH paragraph explains the Euler factors at the inert primes. New Remark 3.4, with the script r34_blocks.py, explains the existing Poisson duality: the largest shortfall in the hypothesis occurs where rows and columns both have norm about X, and there the Mobius sieve is the Poisson dual of the carrier energy itself; other blocks also need the hypothesis. Section 5 notes that assumption (T2) is the least secure of the three. The introduction cites the conditional endpoint of Chang and Wang (arXiv:2611.00924) and keeps B* as the reference value. Correction: the zero-density paragraph of Section 4 (and the matching sentences of the abstract and introduction) used a single threshold and wrongly concluded that density estimates give nothing. Splitting rows by the largest real part of their zeros gives excess max(0, 1-2/kappa), under a stated row-count hypothesis and a stated pointwise bound that needs control of 1/L; so kappa < 2.4575 would suffice. De Faveri's zero-density corollary [7, Cor. 1.5] gives excess about 0.284 this way, weaker than 1/4. The refinement of Theorem 3.1 by bramble_trace that the first version-2 submission contained is removed; it will be submitted separately.
title: Quartic Gauss sums with a Möbius carrier, and the large-sieve input a quartic version of the 7/8 method would need
